title: Bidirectional Dijkstra: Porto’s Fastest Street Route
description: Watch how Bidirectional Dijkstra finds the shortest path by expanding search frontiers from both the start and the destination simultaneously. This visualization turns a real street-map graph into a meet-in-the-middle strategy for faster convergence.
ig_caption:
🚦 Porto (Cedofeita) street graph, but make it algorithmic. 🌉

In this reel, **Bidirectional Dijkstra** runs two Dijkstra searches in parallel—one forward from the start node and one backward from the goal node—until the frontiers meet. 🧠✨ By splitting the exploration, it can reduce the number of expanded nodes on weighted graphs compared to a single-direction search, while still guaranteeing **optimal shortest paths**.

Graph theory angle: think of real streets as a **weighted graph** (edges = road segments, weights = distance/time). 🗺️ The moment the forward and backward settled regions overlap, the algorithm can stitch together the best candidate route using the best known distances from both directions.

Want a deeper breakdown of the relaxation + stopping condition? 💡 Hit **like**, follow for more pathfinding, and comment **“MAP”** if you want the next city visualization! 👇
